stories.title: A hybrid CNN-LSTM-transformer model for window-based anomalous transaction detection in financial data
stories.description: Some of the challenges of financial transaction anomaly detection include the fact that fraud is rare, adaptive and costly to operate. In this study, we propose the novel stacked convolutional neural network-long short-term memory-Transformer (CNN-LSTM-Transformer) model to detect anomalous transactions in a window-based approach and empirically analyze it with the public Credit Card Fraud Detection Dataset 2023. The dataset contains 568,630 anonymized records with 28 principal component analysis (PCA)-transformed features and transaction amount. To provide a conservative assessment, controlled imbalance experiments were conducted at transaction-level fraud prevalence of 10%, 5%, 3%, and 1%. Fraud-if-any labeling was adopted for window-level classification because majority voting suppresses rare fraud events in low-prevalence settings. Under the 1% transaction-level fraud setting with window size 16, and averaged over 10 random seeds, the CNN-LSTM-Transformer achieved 97.07% accuracy, 94.42% precision, 85.70% recall, 89.84% F1-score, 95.32% area under the receiver operating characteristic curve (ROC-AUC), and 90.05% area under the precision-recall curve (PR-AUC). Fair baseline comparisons were conducted by training Logistic Regression, Random Forest, and XGBoost on the same flattened window representation. The CNN-LSTM-Transformer performed on par with XGBoost, with no statistically significant difference in F1-score after multiple-comparison adjustment, while both clearly outperformed Logistic Regression and Random Forest; XGBoost retained a small advantage in PR-AUC and precision, and the CNN-LSTM-Transformer achieved slightly higher recall. The results indicate that gradient-boosted trees remain highly effective on PCA-transformed tabular fraud benchmarks, whereas the neural architecture should be interpreted as a window-based representation-learning approach rather than as proof of deployment-ready chronological behaviour modelling.

stories.title: Transport of cytotoxic cyanine dyes coupled to siRNA into hematopoietic cancer cells with CD20-, CD22- or CD33-targeting ELART nanocarriers
stories.description: The efficient and safe transfection of hematopoietic cells is a major hurdle that limits efficacy of therapeutic approaches like RNA-interference. We therefore used our modular ELectrostatic Antibody siRNA Targeted therapy platform (ELART) to develop nanocarriers decorated with antibodies for delivery of siRNA into hematopoietic CD20-, CD22-, or CD33-positive cells. To analyze internalization efficacy into tumor cells, we applied nanocarriers loaded with Cy3- or Cy5-labeled siRNA and reached nearly all target cells within 1–4 h. Exposure to Cy5-labeled non-functional siRNAs resulted in reduction of the mitochondrial membrane potential and reduced viability, as detected in tetramethylrhodamine methyl ester (TMRM) and CellTiter-Glo (CTG) assays. We concluded that with our modular nanocarrier system, we can transport cytotoxic agents such as cyanine dyes when bound to siRNA, as ELART nanocarriers safely complex anionic siRNA electrostatically and releases it intracellularly within the target cell. This proof-of-concept study shows that ELART nanocarriers can transport anti-cancer agents utilizing siRNA as carrier substance.

stories.title: Synergistic Co-Zn dual atomic sites drive C-lignin hydrogenolysis via vicinal C-O cleavage
stories.description: C-lignin, a natural biopolymer of caffeyl alcohol subunits linked by benzodioxane motifs, is an ideal feedstock for direct catechol production. However, its hydrogenolysis is hindered by the high bond dissociation energies and steric congestion of vicinal C–O bonds in benzodioxane structures. Here, we report a low-loaded Co–Zn dual single-atom catalyst (CoSA–ZnSA@NC) that enables efficient C-lignin hydrogenolysis, achieving 84.6% catechol yield, 82% selectivity toward 4-propylcatechol, and a turnover number five times higher than precious Ru/C, attributing to the synergistic effect of the dual atomic sites. The major product, 4-propylcatechol, can be readily purified and upgraded into diverse value-added molecules. Mechanistic investigations reveal that the Zn and Co species, acting as the directing and active centers, respectively, synergistically drive the quasi-concerted cleavage of the vicinal C–O bonds. This work presents an atomically dispersed non-precious metal catalyst for C-lignin hydrogenolysis, providing a sustainable route to well-defined aromatics. C-lignin is an attractive renewable feedstock for producing catechols, but its strong chemical bonds make it difficult to break down selectively. Here, the authors develop a low-loading Co–Zn dual single-atom catalyst that enables efficient C-lignin hydrogenolysis, providing a sustainable route to valuable aromatic chemicals.

stories.title: Artificial neural network-based phase-shift optimization for input ripple minimization in an interleaved boost-Z-source converter
stories.description: This paper presents a neural-network-based phase-shift control strategy for minimizing input current ripple in an asymmetric interleaved Boost–Z-source converter. Unlike conventional fixed-phase interleaving, which provides ripple reduction only at specific operating points, the proposed method adapts the interphase shift according to the converter’s instantaneous duty cycles. A comprehensive ripple-surface mapping was first carried out over a wide range of operating conditions, generating the optimal phase shift required to minimize the RMS of ripple for each duty-cycle combination. These optimal operating points were then used to train a compact 2–10–1 feedforward artificial neural network (ANN) capable of predicting the ripple-minimizing phase shift in real time. The trained network is deployed on a low-cost STM32 microcontroller and integrated into the converter’s PWM generation system. Hardware experiments performed on a full-scale prototype validate the simulation findings and confirm the method’s practicality and robustness. The proposed approach combines the accuracy of data-driven modeling with the simplicity required for embedded implementation, offering a strong alternative to analytical ripple-minimization techniques for asymmetric or hybrid power converter architectures. The method demonstrates fast dynamic response to duty-cycle variations and strong agreement between simulation and hardware results.
